description: Engram's hooks are the entire mechanism by which memory reaches the model without the model asking for it, and the only thing that starts the server the MCP entry talks to. SessionStart runs two commands: ensure-server.sh, which brings up the local HTTP daemon on 127.0.0.1:7433 (idempotent, silent, and always exit 0 — a memory server that will not start makes a degraded session, not a broken one), and the primer. SessionStart fires on startup, resume, /clear, and after a compaction — every point where the agent's context is otherwise empty or thinner than a moment ago — and injects the session primer that names the memory tools and gives the agent a reason to call them. SubagentStart fires at every subagent spawn, including workflow-spawned agents that never came through an Agent tool call, and is the only channel that reaches all of them — SessionStart never fires for a subagent at all. It delivers a shorter primer whose one added point is that a subagent reports back through a summary, and summaries lose what was not written down. Bare stdout is silently discarded on that event, so it returns the hookSpecificOutput envelope; getting this wrong produces no error, just a primer that never arrives. PreCompact fires just before a compaction discards context; it cannot inject anything back (Claude Code exposes no injection channel on that event), so it only records the event to telemetry — the actual 'flush what you know before you lose it' nudge lives in the primer and the recall footer instead, both already seen every session. PostToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit fires after every file change and drops a tiny spool record under the Engram home's queue directory; the hook itself never opens the database (writes stay off the hot path), it only marks that a file changed so a later reindex knows what to look at. All of them exit 0 unless the home is uninitialized, in which case they are no-ops — a plugin installed but never `engram init`-ed does nothing rather than erroring.
